newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Elf Nigeria's new oilfield to start in 199.
newsitem.headline: Elf Nigeria's new oilfield to start in 199.

text.p: Elf Petroleum Nigeria Ltd plans to bring on stream a new offshore oil field in 1998, the company's chief executive, Yngvar Heide, said on Tuesday.
"Our next offshore field Ofon on OML 102 will come on stream in 1998," he told an industry conference in Lagos.

Peak production from the field will be 60,000 barrels per day, representing 30 percent of the output of the joint venture between France's Elf Aquitaine and state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp by the turn of the century.
The joint venture spent $60 million on development costs this year, Heide said.
"Our present planning is to make the offshore field a zero flaring field," he said.
The company is developing a gas project named Obite at a cost of $450 million. "It is from this we would be supplying the 23 percent of gas required by the LNG project," Heide said.
Elf is a partner in the $4 billion Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas plant project being built in the southeastern part of the country and projected to begin delivering gas in 1999.
